## Native compilation audit ? round 1 (read-only)

**Verdict: REVISE**

I read only; I executed nothing. No build, no `--self-test`, no `check-native-workflow.mjs`, no npm/gradle/xcodebuild, no network. Every statement below is from source inspection of the files in `snapshot-1.json` plus the installed Expo 57.0.20 / `@expo/cli` 57.0.22 sources under `apps/mobile/node_modules`.

### 1. Requirements vs. artifacts

| # | Scope requirement | Where enforced | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1 | Android ARM64 release-variant APK | `native-compile.yml:51` (`assembleRelease -PreactNativeArchitectures=arm64-v8a`), `check-native-artifacts.py:18` (`lib/arm64-v8a/libreactnative.so`) | Covered by the command; **not** pinned by the C4 contract |
| R2 | Template debug signing | nothing | **Not verified anywhere** |
| R3 | Android embedded JS | `check-native-artifacts.py:19` (`len > 0`) | Weak, uncontrolled |
| R4 | iOS Release simulator `.app` | `native-compile.yml:75`; `Info.plist` `CFBundleSupportedPlatforms` (`:25`) | Covered by command; `-configuration Release`/`-sdk iphonesimulator` **not** pinned by C4 |
| R5 | iOS embedded JS | `check-native-artifacts.py:29` (`st_size > 0`) | Weak, uncontrolled |
| R6 | Code signing disabled | `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO` in the command | Not confirmed on the artifact |
| R7 | Test identity only, disposable checkout | `prepare-native.mjs:5-16`, `check-native-artifacts.py:11,24,72`, gates/STATUS disclaimers | Good |

### 2. Oracle findings (material)

**F1 ? Android signing is entirely ungated (R2).** `android()` checks manifest magic, DEX, ELF and bundle size; it never looks at `META-INF/*.{RSA,SF}` or the v2 signing block. An unsigned or differently-signed `app-release.apk` passes the oracle while the STATUS/gates text claims "signed with the template debug key". Either check signature presence or drop the signing claim from `NATIVE-COMPILE-GATES.md:3`.

**F2 ? "Embedded JS" is the central claim and has the weakest oracle plus zero control coverage.** A 1-byte `assets/index.android.bundle` or `main.jsbundle` passes. More importantly, `controls()` (`:41-59`) never exercises those two assertions: the four fixtures are (a) non-zip, (b) empty `AndroidManifest.xml`, (c) wrong `CFBundleIdentifier`, (d) empty Mach-O ? (d) fails at line 28 before `main.jsbundle` is ever read. So C1's claim to reject malformed fixtures does not extend to the bundle assertions at all. Add a valid-looking-but-bundle-less APK fixture and a `.app` with a valid Mach-O header and a zero-byte `main.jsbundle`, and assert Hermes magic (`\xc6\x1f\xbc\x03`) or a minimum size rather than `> 0`. Also uncontrolled: non-simulator `CFBundleSupportedPlatforms`, and the `aapt` package-name check (`:70-72`), which lives entirely outside `--self-test`.

**F3 ? C4 does not pin the flags that define the scope.** `check-native-workflow.mjs:35` requires only `assembleRelease` and `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`. Not asserted: `-PreactNativeArchitectures=arm64-v8a`, `-configuration Release`, `-sdk iphonesimulator`, `setup-java` `17`, `platforms;android-36`/`build-tools;36.0.0`, template `57.0.22`, and the artifact paths passed to the checker (`:34` only checks the `python3 ? android ` prefix, so a debug-APK path would pass). The six mutations were chosen to match the existing assertions, so their rejection is not evidence that the ARM64/Release/simulator/toolchain scope is enforced. I traced all six by hand and each does throw under `verify` ? the mechanism is sound, the coverage is narrower than the gates text implies.

**F4 ? the drift guard in `prepare-native.mjs` watches the wrong lockfile.** Line 10/24 snapshot `../../package-lock.json` (repo root), but these jobs `npm ci` in `apps/mobile` against `apps/mobile/package-lock.json`. Prebuild has no reason to touch the root lock, so the assertion is near-vacuous for the package actually being compiled. Compare `package-lock.json` in CWD (the `dependencies`/`devDependencies` comparison at `:22-23` is correctly scoped).

### 3. Build-feasibility risks (each costs a build round out of three)

**F5 ? `aapt` in build-tools 36.0.0 is unverified.** `check-native-artifacts.py:71` invokes `$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/36.0.0/aapt`. `aapt` (v1) has been deprecated for several build-tools cycles; I could not confirm from this repo that it still ships in 36.0.0, and the failure would land *after* the ~30-minute Gradle build. `aapt2 dump badging` produces the same `package: name='?'` line and is definitely present. Low-cost, high-value swap.

**F6 ? `DEVELOPER_DIR: /Applications/Xcode_26.4.1.app` is an unguarded exact-path assumption** (`:64`) applied to every step in the iOS job. If the `macos-26` image ships a differently-pathed Xcode, `pod install` and `xcodebuild` both fail late. A first step running `xcodebuild -version` (or `test -d "$DEVELOPER_DIR"`) fails in seconds instead.

**F7 ? `sdkmanager` (`:49`) runs non-interactively with no license handling.** If either package needs an unaccepted license it blocks on stdin. `yes |` or a `--licenses` pre-step removes the failure mode.

**F8 ? the prebuild dependency assertion may abort on benign template drift.** `updatePackageJson.js:165-243` is *designed* to merge the template's `dependencies` into the project (minus `expo-status-bar`/`expo-splash-screen`), so any template dep the mobile package lacks trips `assert.deepEqual` at `prepare-native.mjs:22`. That is fail-closed and arguably correct with `--no-install`, but I could not enumerate the tarball's dependencies (see limitations), so it is an open round-cost risk. Note also that `updatePkgScripts` (`:270-277`) *will* fire: `scripts.android === 'expo start --android'` and `scripts.ios === 'expo start --ios'` both match exactly, so `package.json` is rewritten every run ? harmless in a disposable checkout, and not covered by the guard.

**F9 ? `spawnSync` timeout of 180 s** (`:18`) covers `npm view` + tarball fetch + config-plugin mods on a cold runner. Tight rather than wrong; a kill wastes a round. 300 s is cheaper than a rerun.

### 4. What I verified positively

- Entry-point resolution is sound: `main: "index.ts"` is preserved (`modifyPackageJson` does not touch `main`, despite its docstring), and `expo/scripts/resolveAppEntry.js` ? `resolveEntryPoint` honors `main`, so the `index.js` default in `react-native-xcode.sh:75` is not reached.
- iOS naming is consistent: `utils/npm.js:159-180` renames tarball *paths* `HelloWorld` ? `sanitizedName('PoppinBuildSpike')` and `renameTemplateAppName.js:125` rewrites contents, so `ios/PoppinBuildSpike.xcworkspace` and the shared `PoppinBuildSpike.xcscheme` are the expected outputs, and `CFBundleExecutable` should match `check-native-artifacts.py:26`.
- iOS Release bundling is not skipped for the simulator: `react-native-xcode.sh:36-58` only short-circuits on `*Debug*`, and Hermes output lands at `$DEST/main.jsbundle` = the `.app` root, matching the checker's path.
- Version coherence: `expo` 57.0.20 depends on `@expo/cli` `^57.0.22`, resolved to exactly 57.0.22 in `apps/mobile/package-lock.json:2722`, matching the pinned template `57.0.22`.
- CI security posture is good: workflow-level `contents: read` with per-job `permissions` asserted absent, `pull_request` (not `pull_request_target`), no `secrets.` anywhere, `persist-credentials: false`, all `uses` pinned to 40-hex SHAs, no `continue-on-error`/`if` escape hatches, `needs: native-contract` enforced. `js-yaml` 4.1.1 is a root devDependency, so `on:` parses as a string key under the YAML 1.2 core schema and the root `npm ci` supplies it.
- `prepare-native.mjs` correctly refuses to run outside a GitHub runner and off-platform (`:5-9`), and both checkers use only stdlib/builtins, so the `apps/mobile`-scoped `npm ci` in the compile jobs is sufficient.
- No overclaiming in `STATUS.md:35` or the gates EVIDENCE fields: all hosted outcomes are marked pending and the test identity is disclaimed as non-production.

Non-blocking: no `concurrency`/`cancel-in-progress` and no path filters, so every push to every branch launches a `macos-26` job billed at 10? ? meaningful against a three-round budget.

### 5. Limitations of this review

1. Read-only, single tool class (Read/Glob/Grep). I ran none of the checks, so C1 and C4 remain unexecuted claims from my side; I reasoned through the six mutations manually.
2. I could not open `expo-template-bare-minimum-57.0.22.tgz` (gzip binary, no extraction available). Therefore the template's `dependencies` (F8), the presence of `android/app/debug.keystore` and the `release { signingConfig signingConfigs.debug }` block (F1/R2), the shipped `.xcworkspace`/scheme, and the Xcode bundling phase's `ENTRY_FILE` wiring are all **expected, not verified**.
3. Runner-image facts ? `aapt` in build-tools 36.0.0, the `/Applications/Xcode_26.4.1.app` path, sdkmanager license state, preinstalled CocoaPods ? cannot be checked from this repo and drive F5?F7.
4. `audit-1.json` is empty; I had no prior-round findings to reconcile against.
5. Gradle/Xcode timing against the 45-minute caps is unmodelled.

### 6. Minimum changes for approval

F1 (verify APK signing or drop the claim), F2 (bundle-absent/empty-bundle fixtures + stronger bundle assertion), F3 (pin arm64/Release/iphonesimulator/Java 17 and the artifact paths, with matching mutations), F4 (guard the mobile lockfile). F5?F7 are one-line round-protection fixes I'd fold in before spending a build round.

NATIVE_COMPILE_REVIEW_RETURNED
